lines.japanese: 火薬のにおいに似た、乾いた寒風が吹きつける夜だった。
lines.english: It was a night of dry, cold wind that smelled like gunpowder.

lines.japanese: 柳木原駅前。最終電車とその走行音が、闇の彼方に吸いこまれてゆく。２５時を回った高架ホームはすべての明かりを落とし、俺の頭の後ろで死んだ蛇のように横たわっていた。
lines.english: Outside Yanagihara Station, the last train and the thunder of its passage vanished into the dark. Past one in the morning, the elevated platforms had put out every light and lay behind me like a dead snake.

lines.japanese: しかし、蛇の腹の下にはまばゆい電飾の銀河が広がっている。週末の柳木原は眠らない街なんだ。
lines.english: But under the snake’s belly stretched a dazzling galaxy of electric lights. On weekends, Yanagihara doesn’t sleep.

lines.japanese: 「あァ？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 飲み屋の冷蔵室みたいに冷えこんだ電話ボックスの中で、俺は受話器に向かって白い息を吹きつけていた。
lines.english: Inside a phone booth cold as a bar’s walk-in refrigerator, I breathed white clouds at the receiver.

lines.japanese: 「ちょ、待て。ぜんぜん意味分かんね。てめ、もういっぺん言ってみろコラ」
lines.english: “Hang on. Wait. That made no fucking sense. Say that again, asshole.”

lines.japanese: 「だーからキャンセルだってば。も帰っていいって。いくら待ってたって、お客さんそこには来ないから」
lines.english: “I *said* it’s canceled. You can go home. The client’s not showing up there, no matter how long you wait.”

lines.japanese: 電話の向こうで、オイルライターのキャップを閉じる呑気な音が聞こえた。あとギターリフのかっこいい洋楽。
lines.english: Over the phone came the carefree click of an oil lighter snapping shut. And some Western song with a killer guitar riff.

lines.japanese: 「おいヒモ、チンピラ、テメふざけんな？　ブッ殺すぞ？」
lines.english: “Hey, you freeloading punk. You fucking with me? I’ll kill you.”

lines.japanese: 俺は静かにゆっくりと告げた（どれだけ相手がひとをナメくさってくれようと、俺には声を荒げるなんて、そんな品のない真似ができない）。
lines.english: I said it slowly and quietly. (No matter how much somebody takes me for a chump, I’m incapable of something as vulgar as raising my voice.)

lines.japanese: 「おーコラ。帰っていいじゃねーんだよ、てめ。帰れねっつーの。もう終電出ちゃったっつーのマジで。見てみろよ時刻表、なんならファックスで７兆枚送りつけんぞコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “Hey, asshole. Don’t tell me I can go home. I *can’t*. The last train’s already gone. Check the schedule. I’ll fax you seven trillion copies if that’s what it takes.”

lines.japanese: 話が違う。俺は電話線を通して仲介人エージに訴えた。
lines.english: This wasn’t the deal. I lodged my complaint with Eiji, the broker at the other end of the phone line.

lines.japanese: 客との待ち合わせは深夜０時に柳木原駅東口、駅ビル一階のアジアンスイーツの店の前──それがエージの指定だった。
lines.english: The meeting was set for midnight at Yanagihara Station’s east exit, outside the Asian dessert shop on the first floor of the station building. Those were Eiji’s instructions.

lines.japanese: だから俺は「右手に競馬新聞」が目印だという客が現れるのを、こうして凍える夜の下で一時間以上も待っていたと言うのに──
lines.english: So here I’d been, freezing my ass off for over an hour, waiting for a client I was supposed to recognize by the horse-racing paper in his right hand—

lines.japanese: ──すでにホームは真っ暗だ。しれっとドタキャンだなんて言われたって、俺には温かな我が家へ帰るすべがない。
lines.english: —and now the platforms were pitch-black. He could cancel on me at the last second like it was nothing, but I had no way to get back to my warm home.

lines.japanese: 「……分かったよ。ああもう、あとでちゃんと払うから、タクシー使っていいよ」
lines.english: “...Okay. God, all right, take a cab. I’ll pay you back later.”

lines.japanese: 俺、発見。電話越しに聞く煙草を吐きだす音は、どれほどの誠意をも台無しにする。
lines.english: A discovery: the sound of somebody exhaling cigarette smoke over the phone destroys any amount of sincerity.

lines.japanese: 「てめ、偉ッそうに……」
lines.english: “Big man, aren’t you...”

lines.japanese: 「つーか、あんな？　自慢だけどな？　んな立て替えられるほどの金が財布に入ってたら、最初からおまえみたいなチンピラの紹介する仕事なんて引きうけてねーんだよ」
lines.english: “And another thing, okay? Not to brag, but if I had enough cash in my wallet to front a cab fare, I wouldn't be taking jobs from a two-bit punk like you in the first place.”

lines.japanese: エージは俺にとって、仲介人その２だ。いわば補欠だ。よっぽど金に困ったときしか関わらないようにしている。
lines.english: Eiji was my number-two broker. A substitute, you might say. I tried to stay away from him unless I was really desperate for cash.

lines.japanese: 「おいおい、俺に当たんなって。仕方ねーだろ、クライアントの都合なんだからあ」
lines.english: “Hey, don’t take it out on me. I can’t help it. The client’s got his reasons.”

lines.japanese: 「あァ？　んだ、都合って」
lines.english: “Huh? What the hell do you mean, ‘reasons’?”

lines.japanese: 「いやあ、お客さん、昼間マトリに連れてかれちゃったらしくてェ」
lines.english: “Well, apparently the narcs picked him up this afternoon.”

lines.japanese: 「マトリ？　なんだそりゃ。珍味か。線香か」
lines.english: “Narcs? What the hell are those? Some kind of snack? Incense?”

lines.japanese: 「麻薬取締捜査官」
lines.english: “Narcotics agents.”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、じゃないよ。だからね、お客さんタイホされちゃったの」
lines.english: “Don’t ‘huh’ me. I’m saying the client got arrested.”

lines.japanese: 「あァっ？」
lines.english: “Huhhh?”

lines.japanese: 「んなあ、気の毒に。あんね、先にパクられてたキメ友にぜんぶ歌われちゃったんだって」
lines.english: “Yeah, poor guy. One of his drug buddies got pinched first and sang like a canary.”

lines.japanese: 「あ～あ～、どんだけ絞られたって自分トコで止めるのがジャンキーとしてのマナーなのにねぇ。やだやだ、これだから友情ってやつは信じちゃいけないよ。まァでも？　所持だけの初犯だから執行猶予は確実……」
lines.english: “Ahh, man. No matter how hard they squeeze you, keeping your mouth shut is basic junkie etiquette. God, this is why you can’t trust friendship. Still, hey, first offense, just possession. A suspended sentence is a sure thing...”

lines.japanese: 「おー、待て。ちょっと待て」
lines.english: “Hey. Wait. Hold it.”

lines.japanese: 「んー？」
lines.english: “Hmm?”

lines.japanese: 「おい。なあ、おい。俺をそういうヤクザな人種に関わらせんなって、おまえに何度も何度も何度も念を押したよなあ？　おう、今回の客は普通の普通の普通のサラリーマンだってオメ言ったよなあ？」
lines.english: “Hey. Hey, listen. How many times did I tell you, over and over and over, not to get me mixed up with that kind of shady fucker? Huh? Didn’t you say this client was a regular, regular, regular office worker?”

lines.japanese: 「うんうん、普通のひとよ？　普通ぅーの証券会社に勤める、普通ぅーのサラリーマンよ？　まあ、海外出張の帰りに、つい日本へアレなものを持ちこんじゃうお茶目な習慣はあった、けれ、どもだ」
lines.english: “Yeah, yeah, he’s regular. A perfectly regular office worker at a perfectly regular securities firm. Though he did have this cute little habit of bringing some questionable stuff back from business trips abroad.”

lines.japanese: 「おー待て。ちょっと待て。おまえ、今日の仕事、ただのパイプテントの設営だって言ったよなァ？」
lines.english: “Hold on. Wait a second. You said today’s job was just putting up a tent with a metal frame, right?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、そうよ？　普通ぅーのご家庭の庭に、普通ぅーのテントを立てるだけの、普通ぅーのお仕事よ？　まあ、ちょっとひとには見せられない植物を栽培するためのテントだったらしい、けれ、どもだ」
lines.english: “Yeah, that’s right. A perfectly regular job, putting up a perfectly regular tent in a perfectly regular family’s yard. Though apparently the tent was for growing some plants they couldn’t exactly show other people.”

lines.japanese: 「おい、おいおいおい糞チンピラ。ちょ待て、待てコラ。なあ。俺は仕事をよこせっつったんだよ。犯罪手伝わせろなんて一言も言ってねーだろ、ブッ殺すぞコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “Hey, hey, hey, you piece-of-shit punk. Hold it right there. I asked you for work. I never said I wanted to help commit a crime. I'll fucking kill you, asshole.”

lines.japanese: 「はぁ？　なんでだよ。テント立てるだけで違法だったら、全国の屋外展示場で逮捕者続出じゃねーか」
lines.english: “Huh? Why? If putting up a tent’s a crime, they’d be arresting people at outdoor exhibition grounds all over the country.”

lines.japanese: 「だいたいおまえ、生意気なんだよ。いちいち仕事選んでんじゃねーや、コミュニケーション不全の内弁慶のくせしてよう」
lines.english: “Besides, you’re too fucking picky. Quit choosing your jobs. You can’t even talk to people, you little tough guy who’s only tough at home.”

lines.japanese: 「うる、うるせえなテメ。うう内弁慶とか言うんじゃねーよ、本人意外と気にしてンだからよ、あァん？　俺ァおまえ、アレだほら、あの、ちょっぴり人見知りが激しいだけだ」
lines.english: “Sh-shut up, asshole. D-don’t say I’m only tough at home. I’m actually kinda sensitive about that, all right? I’m, you know, uh, just a tiny bit extremely shy around strangers.”

lines.japanese: 「はッ、いいんだぜー？　俺の仲介が気に入らないなら、またドカチンでもガードマンでも、まっとうなバイトしてりゃいいじゃねーか」
lines.english: “Hah! Go ahead. If you don’t like the jobs I get you, go back to honest work, hauling bricks or playing security guard.”

lines.japanese: 「のヤロウ、ひとの足元見やがって……てめ、シャイでちょっぴり恥ずかしがり屋のこの俺が、ナウなヤングに囲まれてどんだけ辱めを受けたか、今からテレカ百枚分こんこんと語りはじめんぞコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “Bastard, you know you’ve got me over a barrel... You know how much humiliation a shy, slightly bashful guy like me went through surrounded by all those hip young cats? I’ll start telling you right now. A hundred phone cards’ worth, motherfucker.”

lines.japanese: 「何が辱めだよ、要するに村八分だろ。村、八、分。ほら漢字３つで済むじゃねーか。どだい無理なんだよ、おまえの性格じゃ共同作業はさあ」
lines.english: “What humiliation? They just shut you out. Shut. You. Out. There, three words. You just don’t have the personality for teamwork.”

lines.japanese: 「おい。おいチンピラ。おめ、そーゆー失礼なことはっきり言うんじゃねーよ。わりかし傷付いちゃうだろ」
lines.english: “Hey. Listen, punk. Don’t say rude shit so plainly. It actually kind of hurts.”

lines.japanese: 「あーあー、もういいよ分かったよ。今日の仕事はキャンセルな。はい了解了解、分かった分かった」
lines.english: “Yeah, yeah, fine. I get it. Today's job is off. Gotcha, gotcha. I get it, I get it.”

lines.japanese: 「分かったからおまえ、な、女に買ってもらったスーパー外車で早よ迎えに来い。あのアレ、なんか横っちょに、エラみたいな穴ある真っ赤なクルマだよ。な？　俺アルバトロスの下で待ってっから」
lines.english: “I got it, so get over here and pick me up in that super-fancy import your woman bought you. That thing, the bright red car with those, like, gill holes on the side. Yeah? I’ll wait under the Albatross.”

lines.japanese: 「アホかおまえ。俺は忙しいんだよ。だいたい、んな暇あったら最初からおまえにヤバイ橋なんか渡らせねえって。そうだろドラ。俺たちトモダチジャン」
lines.english: “Are you an idiot? I’m busy. Hell, if I had time, I wouldn’t be making you take those risks in the first place. Right, Dora? We’re friends, man.”

lines.japanese: 「待て。ちょっと待ててめ。ムリクリいい子ぶってんじゃねーよ、おれが悪い子みたいな気分になってくんじゃねーかコノヤロウ。いいから早よ迎えに来いっつーの」
lines.english: “Wait. Hold on, asshole. Quit forcing yourself into the good-guy part. You’re starting to make me feel like the bad guy, you bastard. Just come pick me up already.”

lines.japanese: 「や、ほんと悪り！　マジ勘弁。ほんと俺も迎えに行ってやりてーんだけどさ、いま正念場なんだよ」
lines.english: “No, I’m really sorry! Seriously, give me a break. I’d love to come get you, but I’m at a critical moment here.”

lines.japanese: 「てめ、テキトーこいてんじゃねえぞタコ。パチスロと女の金だけで優雅に暮らしてるヒラのヤクザが、なんでこんな時間に正念場迎えん──」
lines.english: “Don’t feed me that shit, you dumbass. What critical moment can a bottom-rung gangster who lives the high life on slot machines and his woman’s cash be having at this hour—”

lines.japanese: 「エージぃ、バスタオル取ってぇー」
lines.english: “Eijiii, get me a bath towel.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、バカっ！　しっ！」
lines.english: “Ah, you idiot! Shh!”

lines.japanese: 「……おい。おい色ガキ。いまなんか聞こえたぞ」
lines.english: “...Hey. Hey, you horny little shit. I heard something just now.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ？　いやァ……気のせいじゃない？」
lines.english: “Huh? Nah... Wasn’t that your imagination?”

lines.japanese: 「ねえエージぃ、お風呂場にマットあったからあとで遊ぼぉー？」
lines.english: “Hey, Eijiii, there’s a mat in the bathroom. Wanna play on it later?”

lines.japanese: 「ばっ、馬鹿おま、声でかいって！」
lines.english: “Y-you idiot, keep your voice down!”

lines.japanese: 「……おい。おい待てコラ。てめ、いまどこにいんだよ。ちなみに俺は、風呂もベッドも有線もねえ寒空の下だ。おお寒み、うーわマジ寒み、やっべ、ぶるぶるぶるぶるっ」
lines.english: “...Hey. Hey, hold the fuck on. Where are you right now? For the record, I’m out in the cold without a bath or a bed or piped-in music. Ohh, cold. Holy shit, cold. Jesus. Brr-brr-brr-brr.”

lines.japanese: 「おいおい、すっげーな、バナナで釘とか打てんぜ？　現状かなりシベリア入ってんすけど。正直オーロラ見えそーなんすけど。ぶっちゃけセントバーナードとか来てくんないかぎり凍死確定なんすけど」
lines.english: “Hey, hey, this is amazing. You could hammer nails with a banana. Things are getting pretty Siberian here. I’m honestly about to see the northern lights. Frankly, unless a Saint Bernard shows up or something, death by freezing’s a done deal.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、ハハ……だからさ、分かんだろ？　こっちも生活かかってんだよ。あいつ、いまの店やめるとか駄々こねちゃってさ。な、分かって！　ゴメン！　じゃあな！」
lines.english: “Ahh, haha... So, see? My livelihood’s on the line too. She’s throwing a fit about quitting the place where she works. Please, understand! Sorry! Later!”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあなじゃねンだよ、ヒモ野郎。てめ、ちょっと待て。いまからそっち行ってゴムに穴開けんぞコラ。分かってんだよ、どうせいつもの『ラ・アニマ』だろ。三階のお魚さん泳いでる部屋だろ」
lines.english: “Don’t ‘later’ me, you freeloading bastard. Wait the fuck up. I’m coming over to poke holes in your rubbers. I know where you are. The usual La Anima, right? Third floor, the room with the little fish swimming around.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ～……ん～、分かった分かった、分かったから。払うよ、約束してた分は全額払う」
lines.english: “Ahh... mm, fine, fine, I get it. I’ll pay. I’ll pay the full amount I promised.”

lines.japanese: 「たりめーだ、んなの。んーなモンは前提の上で、アンドお迎えに来いつってんだよ。こっちァもう帰る手段がねえつってんの。テメ来ねーなら、いまから俺そっち押しかけて、仲良く三人、川の字で寝んぞコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “No shit. That’s a given, and on top of that I’m telling you to come get me. I’ve got no way to go home. If you don’t come, I’m crashing your party and the three of us can sleep side by side in a nice friendly row, you bastard.”

lines.japanese: 「勘弁しろよォ～……ああもう仕方ねえっ！　違約金としてプラス２０％上乗せ！」
lines.english: “Give me a break... Oh, fuck it! Twenty percent on top, as a cancellation fee!”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、３０パー足す！」
lines.english: “No, make it thirty!”

lines.japanese: 「……ちょっと待て。検討する」
lines.english: “...Hang on. I’ll consider it.”

lines.japanese: 俺は算数が苦手だった（ちなみに国語と理科と社会と英語も苦手なんだけどな）。
lines.english: I was bad at arithmetic. (Also Japanese, science, social studies, and English, for the record.)

lines.japanese: えーと、１２０００の１割が１２００だろ。×３で３６００。元金に加えると……１５６００円か。一晩野宿の慰謝料としては、まあ、悪くない額だ。
lines.english: Okay, ten percent of twelve thousand is twelve hundred. Times three is thirty-six hundred. Add that to the original amount... Fifteen thousand six hundred yen. Not bad compensation for a night out in the cold.

lines.japanese: 「あー、もしもし、エージ君」
lines.english: “Ah, hello, Eiji, my good man.”

lines.japanese: 「だからゴメン、悪りぃけど！　今回のところは許して！」
lines.english: “So I’m sorry, okay? Really sorry! Let me off this once!”

lines.japanese: 「おう許す。つーか全面的に祝福する。ごゆっくりお楽しみください。ラブ・フォーエバー」
lines.english: “Sure, you’re forgiven. Hell, you have my wholehearted blessing. Take your time and enjoy yourselves. Love forever.”

lines.japanese: がちゃん。ぴぴー、ぴぴー、ぴぴー。
lines.english: Clunk. Beep-beep, beep-beep, beep-beep.

lines.japanese: 俺は吐きだされたテレホンカードを引きぬき、とりあえず二度とやつの仕事は受けるまいと決意を新たにして、窮屈なボックスをあとにした。
lines.english: I pulled out the ejected phone card, renewed my vow never to take another job from that bastard, and left the cramped booth.

lines.japanese: 「とは言ったものの……」
lines.english: “That said...”

lines.japanese: ナイロンの安物財布には小銭がわずか。という分かりきっていた事実を再確認して、俺はそれを尻ポケットへ戻した。
lines.english: My cheap nylon wallet held a little loose change. Having reconfirmed what I already knew, I put it back in my rear pocket.

lines.japanese: さて、これから退屈な一夜をいかにして明かしたものかと考えた。
lines.english: Now, how was I going to get through this boring night?

lines.japanese: 見上げればスモッグだらけの曇った夜空は、地上にはびこる不健康な光を浴びて薄紫色に染まっていた。
lines.english: Overhead, the cloudy sky was thick with smog, stained pale violet by the unhealthy light infesting the ground below.

lines.japanese: ぎらつく極彩色のネオン。終夜営業の店が吐きだす白光。行きかう車列の流星。
lines.english: Glaring neon in every lurid color. White light vomited from all-night businesses. Meteor trails from the endless procession of cars.

lines.japanese: 幻想的な夜景──なんて言葉があるけど、夜の柳木原の眺めはその対極に位置する毒々しいリアルの象徴だ。
lines.english: People talk about a “dreamlike nightscape,” but Yanagihara by night was the polar opposite: the very picture of poisonous reality.

lines.japanese: 紫色の空の下、俺は繁華街の音と光に包まれながら、ふらふら泳ぐようにスクランブル交差点を渡った。
lines.english: Under the purple sky, wrapped in the noise and light of the entertainment district, I drifted across the scramble crossing like I was swimming.

lines.japanese: そして、駅から伸びる太い目抜き通りを進んだ。柳木原のメインストリートは、日付が変わったって喧騒に満ちている。
lines.english: Then I followed the broad avenue out from the station. Even after midnight, Yanagihara's main street seethed with noise.

lines.japanese: 立ちならぶデパートやショッピングビルに挟まれた片側三車線のこの道は、国道……えーと、何号だったかな。まあ、いいや。大抵は『花水木通り』っていう通称の方で呼ばれている。
lines.english: Three lanes ran each way between ranks of department stores and shopping complexes. It was National Route... What number was it? Whatever. Most people called it Flowering Dogwood Street.

lines.japanese: 初めて柳木原にやって来るおのぼりさんなら、とりあえずこの筋をぶらつけばいい。そういうところ。
lines.english: If you’re some out-of-towner visiting Yanagihara for the first time, wander along here and you’re set. That kind of place.

lines.japanese: でもひとりで歩くときはちょっとウザいのもいる。とくにそのころはまだ規制が厳しくなる前だったから、すぐにキャッチのにーちゃんや立ちんぼのねーちゃんがまとわりついてきた。俺はすこし速度を上げた。
lines.english: But some people could be a pain when you were walking alone. Especially back then, before the rules got stricter: street promoters and streetwalkers would be all over you in no time. I picked up the pace a little.

lines.japanese: 大通りを逃れて細い道へ潜ると、ちょいと大衆的つーか扇情的つーか、元気なお兄さんやお父さんの集まる柳木原の歓楽街がそこに開ける。
lines.english: Slip off the main road into a narrow street, and Yanagihara’s nightlife district opens up before you. A bit more down-to-earth, or down-and-dirty, where guys and dads with plenty of energy gather.

lines.japanese: ここはピンフ通り。正しくは『へいわ通り』だけど、地元のやつらはみんなそう呼んでる。
lines.english: This was Pinfu Street. Officially it was Peace Street, but every local used the mahjong reading.

lines.japanese: 差しかかった雑居ビルの階段から、浮かれた一団が歩道いっぱいに湧いて出てきた。
lines.english: A boisterous crowd spilled from the stairwell of a mixed-use building and flooded the sidewalk.

lines.japanese: やつらは次なる宴会場が決まらず、タチの悪い寒冷低気圧みたいにぐずぐずとその場に停滞していた。俺はその群れの真ん中を割って突きすすむ。
lines.english: Unable to decide upon their next drinking hole, they stalled in place like an obnoxious cold front. I split their formation and drove straight through the middle.

lines.japanese: 「いてっ」
lines.english: “Ow!”

lines.japanese: 肩になにか当たった。だって、どいてくれないんだから仕方ない。
lines.english: Something hit my shoulder. Well, what else was I supposed to do if they wouldn’t move?

lines.japanese: 「ってえな……おー、待てよ、あんちゃん」
lines.english: “That hurt… Hey. Hold it, buddy.”

lines.japanese: 不可抗力を許せない心狭き男が毒づいた。酔って粋がった仲間が、一緒になってひゅうひゅうと煽りたてる。
lines.english: The narrow-minded fellow, incapable of forgiving an unavoidable accident, spat a curse. His drunken, posturing friends joined in with jeers and whistles.

lines.japanese: 「悪い、勘弁」
lines.english: “Sorry. My bad.”

lines.japanese: 俺は片手を上げて、やつらの戦闘意欲を脇へさばいた。夜のピンフ通りでは、血の気の多い連中を構ってたら時間がいくらあっても足りない。
lines.english: I raised a hand and deflected their urge to fight. Stop for every hothead on Pinfu Street at night and you’d need all the time in the world.

lines.japanese: 「ったく、気ィ付けろ馬鹿野郎……」
lines.english: “Jesus, watch where you’re going, asshole...”

lines.japanese: この界隈は日中ストレスを溜めこんだやつらの為にある一大遊技場。俺と遊ばなくたって、あいつらには暇を潰す手段がいくらでもある。
lines.english: This whole area was one big playground for people who’d spent the day building up stress. They had plenty of ways to kill time without playing with me.

lines.japanese: たとえば居酒屋。たとえばバー。クラブ。カラオケ屋。ボウリング場。オールナイトシアター。インターネット喫茶。レンタルスペース。金で買えるロマンスを否定しない大人なら、選択肢は飛躍的に増える。らしい。
lines.english: A tavern, say. Or a bar. A club. Karaoke. A bowling alley. An all-night movie theater. An Internet cafe. A room for rent. For grown-ups who had nothing against buying romance, the options multiplied dramatically. Apparently.

lines.japanese: それでも行く当てのない大きな子供たちは、煙草に火をつけてその場にしゃがみこむ。マナー知らずの若さがあれば、ストリートはどこだってオープンカフェだ。
lines.english: Big kids who still had nowhere to go lit cigarettes and squatted down on the spot. If you’re young enough not to know any manners, every street’s an open-air cafe.

lines.japanese: 不意に街の片隅から、胃袋を鳴かせる魅力的な匂いが漂ってきた。古びた木目を模した串焼き屋の扉が、食虫植物みたいにぱっくり口を開けて通りかかる獲物を待ちぶせていた。
lines.english: Without warning, an enticing smell drifted from a corner of the city and made my stomach growl. Paneled in imitation aged wood, the door of a skewer joint gaped like a carnivorous plant lying in wait for passing prey.

lines.japanese: そこでふと気付く。そういえば俺は腹が減っている。
lines.english: That was when I noticed: come to think of it, I was hungry.

lines.japanese: そして俺は、持ち合わせが足りなくてもツケで食わせてくれる、仏のようなラーメン屋台をひとつ知っている。
lines.english: And I knew one saintly ramen vendor who would feed me on credit when I came up short.

lines.japanese: しかもそこなら、始発の時間まで居座ることだってできる。常連権限ってやつだ。
lines.english: Better yet, I could stay there until the first train. A regular’s privilege.

lines.japanese: ──決まりだ。俺は向きを変え、目的地までの最短距離を突破することにした。
lines.english: —Settled. I changed direction and decided to cut through by the shortest route.

lines.japanese: ここは『グローヴ街』。グローブ通りでもいい。こじゃれた服屋や飯屋がぎっしり詰まっている若者向けの通り。
lines.english: This was the Grove. Grove Street, if you preferred. A street for young people, packed with stylish clothing shops and places to eat.

lines.japanese: この辺りは、すでに（いくつかの飲み屋を除いて）ほとんどの店が明かりを消していた。眠らぬ夜のド派手な色や音からすこし遠ざかって、ここでは水銀灯のありふれた光さえ慎ましく思えた。
lines.english: Most of the stores around here had already turned off their lights, apart from a few bars. A little way from the sleepless night’s garish colors and noise, even the ordinary light of the mercury lamps seemed modest.

lines.japanese: ひとの姿も極端に減った。昼間は雑踏に隠れているレンガ模様のペーブメントには、菓子の袋や煙草の吸殻やハンバーガーの包装紙があちこち転がっていた。
lines.english: There were far fewer people too. On the brick-patterned pavement, hidden under the crowds by day, snack bags, cigarette butts, and hamburger wrappers lay scattered around.

lines.japanese: 「──だもんでよ、Ｕｈ、うちのチームから活きのいいクルー三人行かせて。そいつら軽く半殺しにしたんだわ、Ｈｕｈ！」
lines.english: “—So, uh, I sent three live wires from our crew. And they only beat those guys half to death, huh!”

lines.japanese: シューズショップのシャッター前。閉店後の店先に排便スタイルでダベっていたのは、老けてるのか実際いい歳なのか、顔の下半分にぱらぱらとヒゲをまぶしたＢ系ファッションの大男たちだった。
lines.english: Outside the shutters of a shoe store, some big men were hanging around after closing, squatting like they were taking a shit. I couldn’t tell if they just looked old or actually were, but the lower halves of their faces were sprinkled with whiskers, and they wore hip-hop gear.

lines.japanese: 西海岸あたりのストリートギャングを模倣した、オーバーシルエットのだぼだぼ服。全部で四人、揃いも揃ってハゲかボーズのまんまる頭、その上にニット帽やら野球帽やら載せている。
lines.english: Huge baggy clothes copied from West Coast street gangs. Four of them, all with round heads, bald or buzzed, topped with knit caps or baseball caps.

lines.japanese: 「したら今度ァ、それ聞いた龍声社の若頭がブッチンいっちゃって。夜中の４時だっつうのに、野郎ソッコー電話かけてきやぁって、ベル鳴る・俺出る・ディスられる？　イン柳木原シティＡＭ４ファッキンミッナイ！」
lines.english: “Then the underboss at Ryuuseisha hears about it and fucking snaps. Four in the morning, and the bastard calls me right away. Phone rings, I’m in, the dissing begins! In Yanagihara City, AM four fuckin’ midnight!”

lines.japanese: 無意味にでかい声でまくしたてられるダミ声のいんちきライムが、聞きたくもない俺の耳に否応なく突きささってくる。もはや騒音公害にも等しいが、仲間たちは手を叩いて、わははクールクールと囃したてた。
lines.english: His fake rhymes, rattled off in an unnecessarily loud, gravelly voice, stabbed their way into my ears whether I wanted them or not. Practically noise pollution, but his friends clapped and laughed, “Cool, cool!”

lines.japanese: 「ビガッ、ビガッ。そんで、そのブチ切れヤクザが電話口でテメエこのガキぁ的なことギャーギャーほざくもんだから俺も、っせえなあ殺すぞダボとか思って、Ｈｕｍ、ま結局あんな大騒ぎンなっちゃったんだけど」
lines.english: “Big up, big up. So this pissed-off gangster’s on the phone screaming all this ‘you little shit’ stuff at me, and I’m thinking, shut the fuck up, I’ll kill you, dumbass. Hmm. Well, that’s how it ended up being such a big fucking mess.”

lines.japanese: 「も、そーゆートコが日本だよな。俺ァさ、そらロスにいたころは毎ンち銃声やら女の悲鳴やら聞いてたよ。でもさ、結局んとこ人種とか宗教とかそういうカテゴライズは意味ねンだよ、Ａｗ、くだらねンだよマジで」
lines.english: “See, that’s Japan for you. Yours truly, back when I was in LA, I heard gunshots and women screaming every day. But in the end, categories like race and religion don’t mean a thing. Aw, it’s bullshit. Seriously.”

lines.japanese: つるぴかのスキンヘッドを上下に揺すって情感たっぷりに語っているのは、黒人さながらに日サロ焼けしているガタイのいい日本人。
lines.english: The hefty Japanese man telling this deeply moving tale, nodding his shiny bald head, had spent enough time in tanning salons to get skin as dark as a Black man’s.

lines.japanese: ぶっとい首にごっついヘッドホンをかけて、会話の合間合間にアーだのハーだの、インタビュー映像の外国人スターみたいな繋ぎ言葉を散りばめているのは、一体どこまでが冗談なんだろう。
lines.english: Heavy-duty headphones hung around his thick neck. All those little “uhs” and “huhs” he sprinkled between sentences, like a foreign star being interviewed on TV—how much of this was supposed to be a joke?

lines.japanese: やけに露悪的な口調で「おれ」と言うときの「れ」が微妙に舌を巻いていた。ぷぷ。俺は思わず歯を噛みしめて笑いをこらえた。ママー、あのおにいちゃん面白いこと言ってるー。しっ、見るんじゃありません。
lines.english: Even the way he said “yours truly” in that overdone bad-boy voice had a funny little roll on the R. Pfft. I clenched my teeth to keep from laughing. Mommy, that man’s saying funny things! Shh, don’t stare.

lines.japanese: 「Ｕｍｍ……なんつうのかな、Ｕｈ、学校とか職場からドロップアウトしてここ集まってきたやつらってなァよ、言ったらみんなファミリーみてえなもんじゃん、Ｅｈ？　したらオメー、家族守ンのが俺の美学ー……」
lines.english: “Umm... How do I put it? Uh, guys who dropped out of school or work and gathered here, they’re all like family, right? Eh? So, you know, protecting my family is my cooode...”

lines.japanese: 語尾を引っぱってハゲは言葉を止めた。マイクに見立てた握りこぶしを分厚い唇へ押しつけ、残った手を上下させて重めのリズムを刻みはじめた。
lines.english: The bald man drew out the final word, then stopped. He pressed one fist to his thick lips as though it were a microphone and began pumping the other hand to mark a heavy beat.

lines.japanese: 「ドンドン、カッ！　カ、ドンドドン、カッ！」
lines.english: “Boom-boom, crack! Ck-boom-ba-boom, crack!”

lines.japanese: 「ドンドン、カッ！　カ、ドンドドン、カッ！　抜けがらみたい街に集まった家族！　かけがえのないダチを守るが美学！　ビガッ、セッタッ、ステッパッ聞きな！」
lines.english: “Boom-boom, crack! Ck-boom-ba-boom, crack! Family gathered in a hollowed-out town! Protect my irreplaceable crew, that's the code I lay down! Big up, set up, step up—listen!”

lines.japanese: 「ケチつけるカスな奴ら！　ねじ伏せるタフな俺ら──」
lines.english: “Those trash-ass fools who diss our crew! We’re tough, we’ll put the screws to you—”

lines.japanese: ぴたっ、とダジャレ豚のダジャレ小唄が止まった。やばい、ちょっと吹いちゃったのがバレたのかもしれない。だったら面倒なことになりそうだ。俺はゴホゴホ咳きこんで風邪のふりをしながら速度を上げた。
lines.english: The punning pig's little pun-rap stopped dead. Shit. He might have noticed me snort. That would mean trouble. I broke into a fit of coughing, pretending to have a cold, and quickened my pace.

lines.japanese: どうしたと尋ねる仲間たちを片手で制すと、ハゲはその手でホッケージャージのポケットからヴンヴンうなる携帯電話を抜きだした。フリップを開く。すぐに喉を鳴らすような呻き声が続いた。
lines.english: Waving a hand to quiet his friends’ questions, he used it to pull a buzzing cell phone from his hockey jersey pocket. He flipped it open. A throaty grunt followed at once.

lines.japanese: 「Ｕｍ……皇帝からだ」
lines.english: “Um... It’s the Emperor.”

lines.japanese: 成人式で偉いおっさんが喋りだしてもシカトしてそうなコワモテの肥満児たちが、その一言で意外なほどあっさり静かになった。
lines.english: These fat, scary-looking kids seemed like the type who’d ignore some bigwig giving a coming-of-age speech, but that one word shut them up surprisingly easily.

lines.japanese: ダジャレ豚はひとつ咳払いしてからケータイを耳に当てた。だぶだぶの袖から覗く真っ黒い前腕に、蛇のようなタトゥーが彫りこんであった。
lines.english: The punning pig cleared his throat and put the phone to his ear. On the dark forearm peeking out of his baggy sleeve was a snake-like tattoo.

lines.japanese: 「おーう、左右田だァ。ハハー、どしたあカケル」
lines.english: “Yo, Souda here. Haha. What’s up, Kakeru?”

lines.japanese: 気安い薄笑いをコーティングした慎重な声。兄貴肌の元スポーツ選手が若手のホープにマイクを向けるときのような、あの親しげなのにどこかよそよそしい声だ。
lines.english: A cautious voice coated in a casual little smile. Like some big-brotherly retired athlete putting a microphone in front of a promising young player: friendly, yet somehow distant.

lines.japanese: 「あ？　おお、そうだけど……ハァ？　おいおいカケルくんよ、ひょっとしてアンタいま近くにいんのかい」
lines.english: “Huh? Yeah, that’s right... Huhhh? Hey, hey, Kakeru, you telling me you’re somewhere close by?”

lines.japanese: ハゲは胡座をかいていた姿勢から背筋だけ伸ばし、ケータイごと首を左右に振った。だだっ広い胸に垂らしたビッグバックルが揺れて、金メダルみたいに鈍く光っていた。
lines.english: Still sitting cross-legged, the bald man straightened his back and turned his head from side to side, phone and all. The big buckle hanging over his broad chest swayed, glinting dully like a gold medal.

lines.japanese: やべっ。
lines.english: Shit.

lines.japanese: ハゲのでかい目玉が、じろりとこちらへ向いた。もちろん俺は睨みかえすこともなく、平和な小市民らしい臆病さを装い、そそくさとやつらの横を素通りした。
lines.english: The bald man’s huge eyes swung my way. Naturally I didn’t glare back. Acting as timid as any peaceful citizen, I hurried right past them.

lines.japanese: かくして俺は、真夜中のシューズショップをつつがなく行きすぎた。
lines.english: And so I passed the midnight shoe store without incident.

lines.japanese: さらに数歩進んだとき、背後で下卑た笑い声が破裂した。電話の相手がアメリカ帰りのハゲ物語に上手いオチでも付けたんだろうか。心の座布団やるよ。俺は振りかえらずに先を急いだ。
lines.english: Several steps later, crude laughter exploded behind me. Maybe the man on the phone had supplied a decent punchline to the bald guy's Tales of America. I'd give him a point for that one. I hurried on without looking back.

lines.japanese: それからしばらく歩きつづけていると、冷たい冬の夜風に乗って俺の耳に届く音があった。
lines.english: After I’d walked a while longer, a sound reached my ears on the cold winter wind.

lines.japanese: からここ、からここ、こんここん……
lines.english: Kara-koko, kara-koko, kon-ko-kon...

lines.japanese: 打楽器……たぶん太鼓の一種だと思うけど、小学校の鼓笛隊が鳴らすような耳慣れた音とは違う。手のひらで直接叩いてるような甲高い硬質音。
lines.english: Percussion... Some kind of drum, probably, but not the familiar sound of an elementary-school marching band. A hard, high sound, like it was being struck directly with somebody’s palms.

lines.japanese: 「あァ？　なんだ、こんな時間に……」
lines.english: “Huh? What the hell, at this hour...”

lines.japanese: 毒づいてはみたものの、近所迷惑な見えない奏者は、意外に心地よいリズムを刻んでいた。異国情緒たっぷりのエイトビートがいい感じで腹に響く。
lines.english: I grumbled, but the invisible musician making a nuisance of himself was actually keeping a pretty pleasant rhythm. The exotic eight-beat thumped nicely in my stomach.

lines.japanese: 夜更けのグローヴ街に響くエキゾチックな鳴り物を行進曲代わりに、俺は目指す屋台への道のりをショートカットして、細く薄汚い路地に潜りこんだ。
lines.english: Using the exotic percussion ringing through late-night Grove Street as my marching tune, I took a shortcut to the cart down a narrow, grimy alley.

lines.japanese: そのとば口は、古着屋と金融会社の無人契約店に挟まれた幅のせまい空間。湿っぽい暗がりには、誰かの吐瀉物を薄めて気化させたような、饐えた汚臭が漂っていた。
lines.english: The entrance was a tight gap between a used-clothing store and an unattended loan office. The damp darkness smelled sour and filthy, like somebody’s vomit had been watered down and vaporized.

lines.japanese: からここ、からここ、こんここん……からここ、からここ、こんここん……
lines.english: Kara-koko, kara-koko, kon-ko-kon... Kara-koko, kara-koko, kon-ko-kon...

lines.japanese: 太鼓の音が近付いているのか遠のいているのかは……どうだろう、よく分からなかった。
lines.english: Was the drumming getting closer or farther away...? Hard to say. I couldn’t really tell.

lines.japanese: しかし、ねっとりとした空気をかきわけて数歩進んだとき、不意に聴覚がべつの気配を捕えた。
lines.english: But a few steps into the thick air, my ears suddenly picked up something else.

lines.japanese: 足音が、付いてくる。
lines.english: Footsteps. Following me.

lines.japanese: なんだ、いつからだ。くそ、ノリのいい太鼓にばかり気を取られていた。
lines.english: What? Since when? Shit, I’d been too busy listening to that catchy drumbeat.

lines.japanese: 俺は歩きつづけながら後ろ頭をがしがし掻いた。向けられる視線すべてを睨みかえしていたころなら、学校の中でも外でもいつだって気を張っていたから、こんな不覚を取ることはなかった。すっかり平和ボケだ──
lines.english: I scratched the back of my head as I walked. Back when I’d glared at everyone who looked at me, I’d always been on edge, at school or outside. Nobody would’ve caught me off guard like this. Peace had made me soft—

lines.japanese: ──いや、いいことなんだろうけど。むかし近所の偉そうなじいさんが言ってた。剣を取るものは皆、剣で滅びる。
lines.english: —though that was probably a good thing. A self-important old man in my neighborhood used to say that all who take up the sword perish by the sword.

lines.japanese: 世界が平和でありますように。
lines.english: *May peace prevail on Earth.*

lines.japanese: 俺はカビの生えかけた古い記憶を鼻息で吹きとばして意識を集中、耳を後方に傾ける。
lines.english: I snorted the moldy old memory from my mind, focused, and cocked one ear behind me.

lines.japanese: 間違いない、たしかに付いてくる。忍び足というほどではなかったが、あきらかに靴音を立てないよう気を配っている。二人……三人……四人だ。そしてささやき声。若い男の声だった。
lines.english: No mistake. They were definitely following. Not quite tiptoeing, but they were clearly trying to keep their shoes quiet. Two... Three... Four. Then a whisper. A young man’s voice.

lines.japanese: すぐに俺は、靴屋の前でたむろしていたギャング気取りのデブたちを思いだす。若い四人……数も合う。
lines.english: Right away I remembered the fat wannabe gangsters hanging around the shoe store. Four young guys... The numbers matched.

lines.japanese: なんだクソが。やっぱり因縁をふっかけないと気が済まなかったのか。あるいは俺の立ち居振舞いがあまりに優雅なものだから、どこか良家のご子息とでも勘違いされたのかもしれない。
lines.english: What the fuck? Couldn’t let it go without starting shit after all? Or maybe my movements were so elegant they’d mistaken me for the son of some fine family.

lines.japanese: はあ……。
lines.english: Haaah...

lines.japanese: ひそかに白い溜息をこぼした。何が困るって、とにかく俺は、お巡りさんがやって来るような面倒を起こしたくないんだ。
lines.english: I let out a quiet white sigh. The thing was, I really didn’t want to cause any trouble that would bring the cops around.

lines.japanese: 路地の先に目を凝らした。開けた大通りに出るまで２０メートル足らずだ。問題ないだろう、たぶん走れば逃げられる。自慢だけど、俺はわりと脚が速い方なんだ。
lines.english: I peered ahead down the alley. Less than twenty meters to the open main road. Should be fine. I could probably get away if I ran. Not to brag, but I’m pretty fast on my feet.

lines.japanese: ピッ。
lines.english: Beep.

lines.japanese: ふと耳をかすめたのは小さな電子音。後ろからだ。おそらく携帯電話の操作音……いやな予感がした。
lines.english: A faint electronic sound grazed my ears. Behind me. Probably somebody pressing a button on a cell phone... I had a bad feeling.

lines.japanese: 俺は薄汚い臭気を裂いて全速力で駆けだした。
lines.english: I tore through the filthy air at a sprint.

lines.japanese: からここ、からここ、こんここん……からここ、からここ、こんここん……
lines.english: Kara-koko, kara-koko, kon-ko-kon... Kara-koko, kara-koko, kon-ko-kon...

lines.japanese: 夜空の向こうでは太鼓のリズムが激しく震えていた。
lines.english: Across the night sky, the drumbeat trembled fiercely.

lines.japanese: 走りながら肩越しに振りかえる。闇の中で視線がぶつかった。予想通りあいつらだった。
lines.english: Still running, I looked over my shoulder. Our eyes met in the darkness. As expected, it was them.

lines.japanese: 連中は走ってこないが、しかし歩みを止めることもない。ゆっくり距離を詰めてくる。Ｂボーイファッションで装ったギャング気取りの悪人面に、狩猟者まがいの薄笑いが張りついていた。
lines.english: They did not run, but neither did they stop. They closed the distance at a walk. Predatory smiles clung to the ugly faces of the would-be gangsters in B-boy gear.

lines.japanese: その余裕とさっきの電子音、俺は走りながらその意味を考えた。
lines.english: As I ran, I thought about what their confidence and that electronic beep meant.

lines.japanese: 靴屋の前で電話に出たハゲ。あのときやつは、通話相手のカケルとかいうやつが近くにいるような口ぶりだった。つまり──
lines.english: The bald man who’d answered the phone outside the shoe store. He’d sounded like the guy on the other end, Kakeru or whatever, was nearby. In other words—

lines.japanese: ──そいつがこの先どこかで待ち伏せしている、ってことか。
lines.english: —so that meant he was somewhere up ahead, waiting to ambush me?

lines.japanese: 俺は走りながら顎を下げて腰を落とした。重心を落として臨戦体勢、しかし速度は落とさない。
lines.english: I tucked my chin and lowered my hips as I ran. Center of gravity down, ready to fight, but without slowing.

lines.japanese: からここ、からここ、こんここん！　からここ、からここ、こんここん！
lines.english: Kara-koko, kara-koko, kon-ko-kon! Kara-koko, kara-koko, kon-ko-kon!

lines.japanese: 光が近付く。あと５メートル。４メートル。３、２、１、０！
lines.english: The light drew near. Five meters. Four. Three, two, one, zero!

lines.japanese: 俺は右脚いっぱいのバネを使ってコンクリートを蹴った。そして──
lines.english: I kicked off the concrete with every ounce of spring in my right leg. And then—

lines.japanese: 「うるァ！」
lines.english: “Raaah!”

lines.japanese: ──予測どおり明るみから踊りでてきた敵意の影に、加速と体重の載ったスニーカーの爪先を埋めこんだ。
lines.english: —just as predicted, a hostile shadow sprang from the light. I buried the toe of my sneaker in him with all my speed and weight behind it.
“Bwah!”

lines.japanese: パシリ顔の若いロンゲが仰向けにふっとぶ。路地を抜けて飛びだした大通りには、あの極彩色の光と音が氾濫していた。
lines.english: A long-haired kid with *born errand boy* written all over his face flew onto his back. Beyond the alley, the avenue overflowed with that same riot of color, light, and sound.

lines.japanese: 俺は着地した勢いを殺さないまま次の足を踏みだし、倒れた伏兵が立ちあがるより先に、素早くその横を駆けぬけていった。
lines.english: Without losing the momentum of my landing, I took another stride and raced past the fallen ambusher before he could get up.

lines.japanese: 「ペガ、あいつは！？」
lines.english: “Pega! Where is he?!”

lines.japanese: 「あつぅ……すんません逃げられました、あの、あっちに……」
lines.english: “Ow... Sorry, he got away, um, over there...”

lines.japanese: 「ああッ！？　あっちじゃねえよ、早よ追えや新入り！　カケルからの命令なんだぞコレぁ、しくじったら殺されンぞ！」
lines.english: “What?! Don’t ‘over there’ me! Get after him, new guy! These are Kakeru’s orders! Fuck this up and he’ll kill us!”

lines.japanese: どうやら待ち伏せてたのが“カケル”ではなかったらしい。走りながら肩越しに振りかえった。路地裏を抜けてきた真ん丸ボーズたちが、倒れたロンゲに手も貸さず俺のあとを追ってくるようだった。
lines.english: Apparently the guy waiting in ambush hadn’t been “Kakeru.” I looked back over my shoulder as I ran. The round-headed buzzcuts coming out of the alley seemed to be chasing me without even helping the long-haired guy up.

lines.japanese: 「クソが。なに付いてきてんだよ」
lines.english: “Shit. Why are you following me?”

lines.japanese: 繰りかえすけど、脚にはわりと自信がある。騒然とする通行人の林をすり抜けながら、俺はぐんぐんスピードを上げた。
lines.english: Like I said, I’m pretty confident in my speed. Slipping through the forest of alarmed pedestrians, I ran faster and faster.

lines.japanese: そして付けくわえるけど、持久力の方にだって自信がある。親の脛をしゃぶりながらファッション感覚で粋がってる連中とは鍛え方が違う。追ってくる複数の靴音は徐々に遠く離れていった。
lines.english: And let me add, I’m confident in my endurance too. I train differently from guys who live off their parents and wear toughness like a fashion accessory. The several pairs of shoes pursuing me gradually fell far behind.

lines.japanese: 赤信号に直進を遮られたところで、人ごみにまぎれて角を曲がる。そのあとは少しずつ速度を落としながら、適当にいくつか右折と左折を積みかさねた。
lines.english: A red light kept me from going straight, so I blended into the crowd and turned a corner. After that, I gradually slowed down, taking a few random lefts and rights.

lines.japanese: 気が付けば、あのアフリカ太鼓の音が届かない場所にいた。追跡者たちの足音ももう聞こえない。
lines.english: Before I knew it, I was somewhere I couldn’t hear that African drum anymore. The pursuers’ footsteps were gone too.

lines.japanese: 「はぁ……はぁ……はぁ……」
lines.english: “Hah... hah... hah...”

lines.japanese: 俺は脚をとめて呼吸を整えた。
lines.english: I stopped to catch my breath.

lines.japanese: そこはメインストリート『花水木通り』の延長上だったが、もはや駅周辺の喧騒からは遠かった。
lines.english: I was still on the extension of Flowering Dogwood Street, but the clamor surrounding the station lay far behind.

lines.japanese: はるか頭上にはクレジット会社のサイン看板が鮮やかに瞬いているけれど、地上では閉店後のファッションビルが死んだように眠っている。
lines.english: High overhead, a credit company’s sign flashed brightly. Down here, the fashion complex lay asleep after closing, like something dead.

lines.japanese: 「はぁ……はぁ……」
lines.english: “Hah... Hah...”

lines.japanese: 運送会社のトラックが歩道に落としていく低い唸りを聞きながら、俺は肩で息をしていた。
lines.english: I stood heaving for breath while a delivery truck spilled its low growl across the sidewalk.

lines.japanese: 「なんで俺が逃げなきゃなんねーんだよ……世紀末もとっくに過ぎたっつーのに物騒な……」
lines.english: “Why the hell do I have to run away...? The end of the century’s long gone, but it’s still fucking dangerous...”

lines.japanese: 呼吸を整えながらビルの壁面に手を付く。ショウケースの黒いガラスから、夜の冷たさが汗ばんだ手のひらへ伝わってきた。
lines.english: Catching my breath, I put a hand against the building. The night’s cold passed from the black display-window glass into my sweaty palm.

lines.japanese: 実にくだらない災難だった。柳木原にもまだああいう頭の弱い蛮族がいたのか。いや、いるだろうけど。いつの時代もアウトローを気取りたがる男の子は絶滅しない。
lines.english: What a pointless disaster. Yanagihara still had dim-witted barbarians like those? Well, of course it did. Boys who wanted to play outlaw would never go extinct, whatever the age.

lines.japanese: しかし……引っかかる点がひとつ。デブ共のリーダーっぽいツルッパゲが妙なことを言っていた。俺を襲ったのはカケルだかいうやつの指示だと。
lines.english: But... Something bothered me. The cue ball who seemed to lead the fat guys had said something strange. That they’d attacked me on the orders of this Kakeru guy.

lines.japanese: カケル。知らない名前だ。俺に恨みを持つ人間がどこかにいたって不思議じゃないが、しかしカケルなんてやつは知らない。知らないあいだに恨まれていたのか。それとも一体なんだって言うんだろう。
lines.english: Kakeru. Didn’t know the name. It wouldn’t be strange if somebody out there had a grudge against me, but I didn’t know anybody called Kakeru. Had I made an enemy without knowing it? Or what the hell was going on?

lines.japanese: 「はぁ……はぁ……」
lines.english: “Hah... Hah...”

lines.japanese: 俺はガラスに手をついたまま、ゆっくり頭を上げた。暗いショウケースに、今は遠いネオンの集落が反射して映りこんでいた。
lines.english: Keeping one hand against the glass, I slowly raised my head. In the dark display window shimmered the reflection of that now-distant village of neon.

lines.japanese: 「そそるじゃねえかァ……」
lines.english: “Now that's tempting...”

lines.japanese: 突如。闇から染みでてきた、吐息混じりのかすれ声。
lines.english: Without warning—a breathy rasp seeping from the dark.

lines.japanese: 俺は目を見張った。
lines.english: My eyes widened.

lines.japanese: ぬばたまの夜に黒光りするウィンドウ。着飾ったマネキンのちょうど頭の位置に、道化の仮面じみた微笑が重なっていた。
lines.english: A display window shining black in the pitch-black night. Right over the head of a dressed-up mannequin was a smile like a jester’s mask.

lines.japanese: 俺は横に飛びのきながら身をひるがえした。不覚、完全に不意をつかれた。その男はまるで夜の中から染みでてきた鬼火のように、ゆらゆらと肩や頭を揺らめかせて息づいていた。
lines.english: I jumped sideways and spun around. Careless. He’d caught me completely off guard. The man swayed and breathed, head and shoulders wavering like a ghost light seeping out of the night.

lines.japanese: 「ハハハ！　いい……脚だなァ……」
lines.english: “Hahaha! Nice... legs you’ve got there...”

lines.japanese: 喉を潰したようなかすれ声が、白い吐息となって夜に溶ける。
lines.english: His voice, hoarse as if his throat had been crushed, turned to white breath and dissolved into the night.

lines.japanese: 男は長身だった。上から下まで、値段と品質の高さがぎらぎら滲みでた嫌味なハイブランドで全身固めている。荒々しくうねった髪は、アッシュ系のくすんだゴールド。その襟足を毛足の高いファーが覆っていた。
lines.english: The man was tall. Head to toe, he was decked out in obnoxious designer brands that glittered with their price and quality. His wildly curling hair was a dull, ashy gold. Deep fur covered the back of his neck.

lines.japanese: どこかの高級クラブのナンバーワンホストみたいだ。きらびやかなシャンデリアの光を弾くグラスタワーに、プラズマＴＶよりも高いプラチナ色の発泡ワインを注ぐ、そんなシーンの浮かぶ洗練された野性味があった。
lines.english: He looked like the top host at some luxury club. He had a polished wildness that conjured chandeliers flashing off a tower of glasses while platinum-colored sparkling wine—worth more than a plasma TV—poured down it.

lines.japanese: 「少しィ……話をしないかァ……」
lines.english: “How about... a little taaalk...”

lines.japanese: 重たげなまぶたの下で、ぎろりと目玉が動いた。氷を削るような薄いかすれ声は何の冗談だろうか。いちいち語尾が一拍伸びる。絡みつくような嫌らしい喋り方をするやつだった。
lines.english: His eyes shifted beneath heavy lids. What was with that thin, hoarse voice, like ice being scraped? He dragged out every sentence ending by a beat. An unpleasant way of talking that seemed to wrap itself around you.

lines.japanese: 「なに。おまえ誰」
lines.english: “What? Who are you?”

lines.japanese: 俺は率直に聞いた。しかし知りたいのは相手の素性ではなく、気配を殺して俺に近付いてきた真意だった。
lines.english: I asked him straight out. But what I wanted to know wasn’t who he was. It was why he’d sneaked up on me without a sound.

lines.japanese: 「あァーア……鳳、翔だ……おまえに興味を持った……」
lines.english: “Aahh... Kakeru Ohtori... You caught my interest...”

lines.japanese: 不安定にぐらぐら揺れる頭の下、噛みしめた唇の端が吊りあがった。首が不自然な方向へ傾く。瞳孔の開いたような黒目が、充血した白目の中で爛々と輝いている。何かにとり憑かれたホラー映画の端役みたいだ。
lines.english: Beneath the head rocking unsteadily to and fro, one corner of his clenched mouth rose. His neck tilted at an unnatural angle. Pupils black as though blown wide shone feverishly in bloodshot eyes. He looked like some bit player possessed in a horror film.

lines.japanese: 「てめえか」
lines.english: “So it’s you.”

lines.japanese: オオトリカケル。俺を襲わせたというそのクソ野郎を改めて凝視した。嘲るようにおぞましく笑っているその凶悪なイケメン面に、俺は覚えが──
lines.english: Kakeru Ohtori. I took another hard look at the bastard who had supposedly ordered the attack on me. That viciously handsome face wore a hideous, mocking smile, and I remembered—

lines.japanese: ──ない。こんなやつは知らない。少なくとも俺の記憶にはない。
lines.english: —nothing. Didn’t know the guy. At least, not as far as I could remember.

lines.japanese: 「ククク、なぜ逃げたァ……」
lines.english: “Heh heh heh. Why’d you ruuun...”

lines.japanese: 「あァ？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: そいつ、鳳は、腫れたような目蓋を大きく開いた。長身から見下ろしてくるぎらついた眼光は、ひどく威圧的だった。
lines.english: This guy, Ohtori, opened his swollen-looking eyelids wide. The fierce look he cast down from his height was seriously intimidating.

lines.japanese: 「あの程度の雑魚、握りつぶした方が早ええだろう。なぜ逃げた、おまえは育ちがいいんだなァ」
lines.english: “It’d have been quicker to crush small fry like those. Why’d you run? You must’ve been raised riiight...”

lines.japanese: 「てめ、見てたのかよ」
lines.english: “You were watching?”

lines.japanese: どこから尾けられてたんだろう。美人のねーちゃんでもないやつにケツを追いまわされていい気はしない。俺は壁沿いに距離を取りながら一言発した。
lines.english: Where had he started tailing me? Having somebody chase my ass didn’t feel good unless it was a pretty woman. I edged away along the wall and spoke.

lines.japanese: 「関係ねえだろ」
lines.english: “None of your business.”
“Hah!”

lines.japanese: やつは首の据わってない赤ん坊みたいに頭をぐらつかせながら、大袈裟に鼻で笑った。
lines.english: He gave an exaggerated snort, head wobbling like a baby’s that couldn’t hold itself up yet.

lines.japanese: 「構えるなよ。おまえを試したことは謝ろう、ささやかな好奇心だ、許せ野良犬」
lines.english: “Don’t get ready to fight. I’ll apologize for testing you. Just a little curiosity. Forgive me, stray dog.”

lines.japanese: 「許せじゃねえよ狂犬、テメなにが『謝ろう』だコラ、命令形の謝罪なんて聞いたことねえよコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “Don’t fucking order me to forgive you, rabid dog. What’s this ‘I’ll apologize’ shit? Never heard an apology in the form of an order, you bastard.”

lines.japanese: 「おい。おい酔いどれホスト。おまえだよな、俺にあの駄洒落ブタ仕掛けたの。なあ？　あァ？　どーゆーつもりだテメ、揺れてる場合じゃねえよ、傷害教唆で訴えんぞコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “Hey. Listen, drunken host. Yeah, you. You're the one who sicced that punning pig on me, right? What the fuck were you thinking? Quit swaying and answer me. I'll have you charged with inciting assault.”

lines.japanese: 「クク！　俺はおまえを認めたんだ、そう腹を立てるなァ……」
lines.english: “Heh heh! I’ve acknowledged your worth. Don’t be so aaangry...”

lines.japanese: やつは聞き分けのない子供をなだめるような──つまり完全に相手を下位に置いた目線で言った。
lines.english: He spoke as if soothing a child who wouldn’t listen—in other words, looking at me from a position of complete superiority.

lines.japanese: 「立ててねーよ」
lines.english: “I’m not angry.”

lines.japanese: 警戒しているだけだ。
lines.english: Just on guard.

lines.japanese: 実際、俺の可愛い暴言なんて、口を開けばうっかり出てしまう方言みたいなもんだ。エージやパルさんならとっくに気付いてる。
lines.english: Really, my adorable insults were like a dialect that slipped out whenever I opened my mouth. Eiji and Paru had figured that out ages ago.

lines.japanese: そもそも俺の精神は、ほとんど怒りという感情を生まない。少なくともじいさんと約束して以来は、焦りや苛立ち以上の激情に心を揺すぶられた覚えがないんだ。
lines.english: I hardly ever felt anger in the first place. At least since my promise to the old man, I couldn’t remember being shaken by anything stronger than impatience or irritation.

lines.japanese: このイカれた男の言ったとおり、たしかに俺は育ちがいいのかもしれない。
lines.english: Maybe this lunatic was right. Maybe I really had been raised right.

lines.japanese: 「でオマエ、何がしてえの」
lines.english: “So what do you want with me?”

lines.japanese: 「あ゛あ゛ー？　相談だよ。ハハハ！　おまえ、俺と組め」
lines.english: “Aaah? A proposition. Hahaha! You. Team up with me.”

lines.japanese: 「ハァ？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 鳳がよろめいて一歩出た。釣りあがる口の端、しかし黒々と剥かれた瞳は笑っていない。その薄気味悪い笑顔は親睦のしるしなのか、敵意のあかしなのか。俺はただでさえ人の心を読むのが苦手だった。
lines.english: Ohtori staggered a step closer. The corners of his mouth rose, but his exposed black eyes weren’t smiling. Was that creepy smile a sign of friendliness or proof of hostility? Reading people was hard enough for me already.

lines.japanese: 「なに、組めって」
lines.english: “What do you mean, team up?”

lines.japanese: 「システムやフォーマットは問わねえ……おまえを管理できればそれでいい」
lines.english: “The system, the format, none of that matters... As long as I can keep you under my control.”

lines.japanese: 「なんだこれ。ナンパか」
lines.english: “What’s this? You hitting on me?”

lines.japanese: 「ククッ！　近いな。そう捉えても支障はねえぜェ？」
lines.english: “Heh heh! Close enough. No harm in seeing it that waaay.”

lines.japanese: 鳳の肩が揺れる。俺はやつの所作や言葉から滲みでる刺々しさが、必ずしも殺気や闘争心ではないことに気付いた。それは、もっとその向こうにあるもの──支配欲や征服欲のようなものかもしれない。
lines.english: Ohtori’s shoulders shook. I realized the sharpness seeping out of his words and movements wasn’t necessarily a desire to kill or fight. It might be something further beyond that—a desire to dominate or conquer.

lines.japanese: 「あー、要するにアレか。あの、おまえらのなんか、アホみたいなワルワル軍団に入れっつー話か」
lines.english: “Ahh, so basically, what? Uh, you’re telling me to join that, like, stupid little bad-boy army of yours?”

lines.japanese: 「それでもいい。そうでなくともいい。ともあれ今後は、俺の目の届く範囲にいろ」
lines.english: “That’d do. So would something else. In any case, from now on, stay where I can keep an eye on you.”

lines.japanese: 鳳は俺を睨んだまま、顎を上げて顔を斜めに向けた。いちいち見下ろす視線が不遜で傲慢で高圧的だった。
lines.english: Keeping his glare on me, Ohtori raised his chin and turned his face at an angle. Every look down his nose was insolent, arrogant, overbearing.

lines.japanese: 「……あのさ。マジで意味分かんねーんだけど」
lines.english: “...Look. I seriously don’t know what the fuck you mean.”

lines.japanese: 「いいんだよ、おまえは分からなくても……」
lines.english: “That’s all right. You don’t need to understand...”

lines.japanese: やつの口元をよく見れば、言葉を止めたときの下顎が細かに震えていた。肩や頭はふらふらと不安定に揺れっぱなし。週末の夜はタチの悪い酔っ払いが多くて困る。
lines.english: Looking closely at his mouth, I saw his lower jaw trembling faintly when he stopped speaking. His head and shoulders kept swaying unsteadily. Too many nasty drunks out on weekend nights. What a pain.

lines.japanese: 「まずは俺と組め。俺の一部になれ。俺から逸れるな」
lines.english: “First, team up with me. Become part of me. Don’t stray from me.”

lines.japanese: 男の言葉が熱を帯びてゆく。その暑苦しさに、かえって俺は冷めてしまう。
lines.english: Heat entered the man’s words. And the more overheated he got, the cooler I felt.

lines.japanese: 「……おまえアレだ、飲み過ぎだ。ほら、便所行って喉に指突っこんで来い。えぅ～ってなるから、えぅ～って」
lines.english: “...You know what? You’ve had too much to drink. Go stick your fingers down your throat in the bathroom. You’ll go ‘urrgh.’ Like, ‘urrgh.’”

lines.japanese: 「ヴァガヤロ吐きだすものなんざァ、はーッ！　貴様への言葉しかねえなあ！」
lines.english: “Dumbass, there’s nothing for me to spit out—haaah!—but words for you!”

lines.japanese: 「シラフでそれかよ。相当キてんな」
lines.english: “You’re like this sober? You’re really fucking gone.”
“Hahahahaha!”

lines.japanese: 鳳は舞台役者みたいに大口を開けて、あのかすれた声で高らかに笑った。いちいち芝居がかったやつだ。
lines.english: Ohtori opened his mouth like an actor onstage and laughed grandly in that rasping voice. Every inch of him was theatrical.

lines.japanese: 「あ゛～？　そりゃあお互い様だよなあ！　おまえ、俺によく似た目をしてるぜえ！」
lines.english: “Aahh? That makes two of us! You’ve got eyes a lot like miiine!”

lines.japanese: 「あァ？　ふざけんなコノヤロウ。てめーらみたいな、いい歳こいたアダルトヤンキーと一緒にすんじゃねえよ。こちとら、そーゆーヤンチャは思春期入り口で卒業してんだ」
lines.english: “Huh? Fuck off, you bastard. Don’t lump me in with overgrown delinquent assholes like you. I graduated from that kind of troublemaking when I was barely into puberty.”

lines.japanese: 「ヒハハ、つれねえなあ！　じゃれあおうぜ、なあ、××××同士！」
lines.english: “Hee-haha, so cold! Let’s play, come on, we’re both ****!”

lines.japanese: 語尾が伸びない。ファー付きコートのたっぷりした裾が、風を孕んで膨れあがった。
lines.english: He didn’t stretch out the last word. The ample hem of his fur-trimmed coat caught the wind and billowed out.

lines.japanese: 速い。それは修練を積んだ身のこなしだった。一歩の踏み出し、わずかそれだけで察知させるほどに。
lines.english: Fast. And trained. A single step told me that much.

lines.japanese: 「くッ」
lines.english: “Ngh!”

lines.japanese: こいつはデキる。近付かれては危険だと直感し、だが後ろは黒水晶の壁、俺は重心を沈めてサイドへ跳んだ。
lines.english: This bastard knew what he was doing. Instinct warned me not to let him close, but the black-crystal wall stood at my back. I dropped my center of gravity and sprang sideways.

lines.japanese: それで距離は保てたが、しかし次の瞬間、やつの右手には刃物の光が鈍く浮かんでいた。
lines.english: That kept the distance between us. But the next instant, a blade’s dull gleam appeared in his right hand.

lines.japanese: 水銀灯の下で睨みあう若者ふたり、一方の手には抜き身のナイフ。そう多くはない通行人が、足を止めて慄然としていた。
lines.english: Two young men glared beneath the mercury lamp, one with a bare knife in his hand. The few passersby stopped in horror.

lines.japanese: 「おい。おい、ふざけんなてめ。やべえもん出してんじゃねえよ」
lines.english: “Hey. Don’t fuck around. Put that shit away.”

lines.japanese: 俺は若干の前傾姿勢から、顎を引き、相手を睨みあげ、両こぶしを前後に並べて攻守の構えを取った。
lines.english: Leaning slightly forward, I tucked my chin, glared up at him, and set one fist before the other, ready to attack or defend.

lines.japanese: 「ほう……ボクサースタイルか……」
lines.english: “Oh... A boxer’s stance...”

lines.japanese: 「感心しなくていいんだよ、おう、しまえソレ。ご通行中の皆さんから、奇異の視線を集めまくりじゃねえかコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “You don’t need to be impressed. Hey, put that away. We’re getting all kinds of funny looks from members of the passing public, you bastard.”

lines.japanese: 軽く膝を温めながら、慎重に一歩ずつ距離を開ける。やつの光りものは投擲武器でもある、まだ背を向けるには間合いが近かった。
lines.english: Keeping a light spring in my knees, I carefully widened the distance one step at a time. His blade could be thrown as well; we were still too close for me to turn my back.

lines.japanese: 「退くなよ……来いよ……」
lines.english: “Don’t back aaaway... Come ooon...”

lines.japanese: 「アホか。ドン引きだっつうの」
lines.english: “Are you an idiot? You’re making me back the fuck away.”

lines.japanese: 「なァに、リアルファイトじゃないぜえ？」
lines.english: “Oh, this isn’t a real fiiight.”

lines.japanese: 「あァ？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「ほんの見極め……コミュニケイションだよ！」
lines.english: “Just sizing you up... Communicaaation!”

lines.japanese: 鳳が踏みこんだ。モデル並の長い脚は一歩が深い。しかし突きこんできた右腕、刃の先端が向かってくる軌道は馬鹿正直に真正面だ。
lines.english: Ohtori stepped in. With legs as long as a model’s, one stride carried him deep. But his right arm came thrusting at me, the point of the blade traveling on an idiotically direct line.

lines.japanese: 俺は左足を軸に半身を引いた。速いだけの突きが夜を切ってかすめてゆく。その光に目を凝らし、コンマ１秒で通過する烈風をさらに細切れの世界に落としこむ──
lines.english: I pivoted on my left foot and twisted half my body out of the way. The thrust cut through the night and skimmed past, nothing but speed. I fixed my eyes on its gleam, breaking the tenth of a second it took that gale to pass into finer and finer instants—

lines.japanese: ──見えた。鳳の肘が伸びきるわずか一瞬前。そのタイミングにかち合わせて、俺はひねった上体を戻す反動に、右こぶしを乗せて走らせた。
lines.english: —there. The instant just before Ohtori’s elbow fully extended. Matching that moment, I sent my right fist out on the recoil of my twisting torso.

lines.japanese: 「シュ！」
lines.english: “Shh!”

lines.japanese: 重くはないが緻密に照準をしぼったフックが、ナイフを握ったやつの手首を捕えた。鈍い白銀の光が、持ち主の手を離れて夜の底に転がった。
lines.english: A hook, light but precisely aimed, caught his knife hand at the wrist. The dull silver flash left its owner’s hand and rolled to the bottom of the night.

lines.japanese: 言葉を失っていた通行人たちがざわめき始める。武器を落とした鳳は打たれた手首を振りながら、ゆがんだ唇の隙間に噛みしめた歯列を覗かせた。
lines.english: The speechless passersby began to murmur. Ohtori shook his struck wrist, weapon gone, and showed clenched teeth through the gap between his twisted lips.

lines.japanese: 「フシィィィーッ！　驚いたぞ！　貴様も思ったより遊べる男だなハハ、ハハ、ハハー！」
lines.english: “Fshhhh! You surprised me! You’re more fun than I thought! Haha, haha, hahaaa!”

lines.japanese: 笑っている。挑発のつもりなのか、据わらない首をぐりんと不自然な角度に傾け、次いでその重みに引きずられたように身体ごと大きくよろめいてみせた。
lines.english: He was laughing. Perhaps it was meant as provocation. His loose neck rolled to an unnatural angle; then, as though his head's weight dragged the rest of him after it, his whole body lurched wildly.

lines.japanese: 「っとォ……ヨレてる場合じゃねえなあ……」
lines.english: “Whoa... No time to be all wooobbly...”

lines.japanese: やつはこめかみに手首の内側を添え、斜めに倒れていた頭を、パントマイムみたいな１アクションでまっすぐに起こした。
lines.english: He placed the inside of his wrist against his temple and righted his tilted head in one movement, like a mime.

lines.japanese: 「フハァー……」
lines.english: “Fhaaah...”

lines.japanese: 喉を鳴らしながら身を低くする。ぶるっと一度頭を震わせると、充血した半眼が大きく見開かれ、ビー玉みたいな黒すぎる瞳が、俺と落ちた武器とのあいだを何度か往復した。
lines.english: He lowered himself with a growl in his throat. His head shuddered once. His bloodshot, half-lidded eyes sprang wide, pupils black as marbles darting between me and the fallen weapon.
“Hah!”

lines.japanese: 「くそっ……」
lines.english: “Shit...”

lines.japanese: 俺たちは数秒の睨み合いの末、常夜灯の光を照りかえす白刃めがけ同時に駆けだした。
lines.english: After staring each other down for a few seconds, we ran at the same time toward the naked blade reflecting the streetlight.

lines.japanese: やつが上体をかがめ、地面すれすれ右手を伸ばす。ばっくり開いた五本の指は、まさに地上の獲物めがけ急降下する猛禽のようだ。
lines.english: He bent low and stretched his right hand just above the ground. Five fingers spread wide, like a bird of prey diving upon quarry below.

lines.japanese: だが、俺の方がわずか目標に近かった。
lines.english: But I was a little closer to the target.

lines.japanese: 「うらァ！」
lines.english: “Raaah!”

lines.japanese: 走りこみざまのアウトサイドキック。鳳の凶器はガードレールの下を滑りぬけ、鉄の鮫が行き交うアスファルトの大河へ消えた。しかし──
lines.english: An outside-foot kick on the run. Ohtori’s weapon slid under the guardrail and vanished into the great asphalt river where iron sharks swam back and forth. But—

lines.japanese: 「いらねえよ」
lines.english: “Don’t need it.”

lines.japanese: ──やつの右腕は獲物を獲りそこねても失速しなかった。やられた、想定外の方向へ急上昇する猛禽、それは決して慣性の動きじゃない。ナイフを拾うと見せたのはフェイクだった。
lines.english: —his right arm did not lose speed when it missed its prey. He had me. The bird of prey swept abruptly upward along a path no momentum could explain. Reaching for the knife had been a feint.

lines.japanese: 「ぐぶぉっ！」
lines.english: “Gbuuh!”

lines.japanese: 油断していた俺の腹に、鉄球クレーンみたいな一撃があらぬ角度からブチ込まれた。拳固ではなく手刀だったが、どうでもいい、内臓をしぼられるような衝撃に頭が真っ白くなる。
lines.english: A blow like a wrecking ball slammed into my unguarded stomach from a crazy angle. Not a fist, the edge of his hand, but who cared? The impact seemed to wring my guts out, turning my mind blank.

lines.japanese: 「く……シシッ！」
lines.english: “Ngh... Shh-shh!”

lines.japanese: 俺は体が折れまがりそうになるのを一瞬だけ堪え、どうにか牽制のワンツーを見せて敵を下がらせた。
lines.english: For one instant I resisted folding in half, then somehow drove him back with a warning one-two.

lines.japanese: 「ふッ、はッ、ふゥ、はッ……」
lines.english: “Huh, hah, hoo, hah...”

lines.japanese: 姿勢を低くしてガードを固めながら、適当にぬるいストレートをちらつかせて距離と時間をかせぐ。
lines.english: Staying low with my guard tight, I flashed a few halfhearted straight punches, buying distance and time.

lines.japanese: どうする。酔ってんだかイカれてんだか知らないが、このクソ野郎には話が通じない。じいさん、俺は手を出していいのか。
lines.english: What now? Drunk or nuts, I didn’t know, but there was no talking to this fucker. Old man, am I allowed to hit him?

lines.japanese: 「ハッ、息は整ったかあ？」
lines.english: “Hah! Got your breath baaack?”

lines.japanese: 鳳は構えも取らずに背中を丸め、腰より下で両手を広げていた。指の関節を握りこまない、熊手みたいな手の平がこちらに向いている。
lines.english: Ohtori hunched his back without even taking a stance, hands spread below his waist. His palms faced me like rakes, fingers uncurled.

lines.japanese: 野郎から際立った殺気は感じられないが、かえってそういうやつにこそ、悪意なく昆虫の頭をねじ切る子供のような残虐性があるものだ。
lines.english: I didn’t feel any strong intent to kill from him. But it was guys like that who could have the cruelty of a child twisting an insect’s head off without a trace of malice.

lines.japanese: 「もっと遊ぼうぜ！　キシャアー！」
lines.english: “Come on, let’s play some more! Kshaaaa!”

lines.japanese: メタルのシャウトみたいな甲高い奇声をあげて、やつが動いた。無防備に腕を下げたまま走りこんでくる。
lines.english: He charged with a high shriek like a metal singer's scream, his arms still hanging defenselessly low.

lines.japanese: 俺は左のこぶしを前へ伸ばし、右をことさら大きく引いて弓をしぼるように構えた。テメエ来るんじゃねえ来たらドでかいのをお見舞いするぜのポーズ。
lines.english: I extended my left fist and drew the right extravagantly far back, like pulling a bow. The *stay the fuck away unless you want a monster right hand* pose.

lines.japanese: 鳳は体より後ろに提げてきた両手を翼のように広げ、正面で豪快に打ちあわせた。派手な見せ技だ。俺はスウェーで上半身を引いた。夜の冷気が叩きつぶされてクラッカーみたいな音が響いた。
lines.english: Ohtori swept both hands forward from behind him like wings and clapped them thunderously together. Pure showmanship. I swayed my upper body back. The night air crushed between his palms with the crack of a party popper.

lines.japanese: それが号砲となって、敵の猛攻が始まった。
lines.english: That was the starting gun. His furious assault began.

lines.japanese: たっぷり引きしぼった俺の右ストレートをひょいとかいくぐり、ふところへ潜りこんでくる。
lines.english: He ducked neatly under the right straight I’d wound up for and came inside my reach.

lines.japanese: 「ハ、ハッ！　ハァ！　クァ！」
lines.english: “Hah, hah! Haaah! Kwah!”

lines.japanese: ガンガン、ガン、ガン、ガンガン、ガン。やつのラッシュは単発が中心で単純だ。たまにコンビネーションが混じってもせいぜいが二連弾。
lines.english: Bang-bang, bang, bang, bang-bang, bang. His rush was simple, mostly single blows. Even when he mixed in a combination, it was two hits at most.

lines.japanese: しかし一発一発が恐ろしく重い。生半可なガードなどたやすく弾きとばされるし、防いでも鉄パイプを受けとめたみたいに衝撃が骨まで滲みる。ホスト顔でモデル体型のくせに、馬鹿力のパワーファイターだ。
lines.english: But each hit was terrifyingly heavy. Anything less than a solid guard was knocked away easily, and even when I blocked, the impact soaked into my bones like I’d stopped an iron pipe. Host’s face, model’s body, and the brute strength of a power fighter.

lines.japanese: 脇を締めた掌打は、しっかり腰のひねりが入ってて強烈無比。間合いが開けばリーチを活かした伸びのよい張り手、そして返す手で手刀。こっちは遠慮がちに牽制弾を打つだけなのに、野郎はやりたい放題だ。
lines.english: His compact palm strikes carried the full twist of his hips and hit with monstrous force. If the distance opened, he used his reach for a long, driving slap, then cut back with a knife-hand strike. I was firing polite little warning shots while the bastard did whatever he pleased.

lines.japanese: 「いっ、痛てっ、痛てえよバカ。待てって、やめろって。見てるから。ご通行中の皆さん見てるから」
lines.english: “Ow, ow, that fucking hurts, idiot. Wait, stop. People are watching. Members of the passing public are watching.”

lines.japanese: 「なら止めてみろ！　さもなくば無様に膝をつけ！　ヒャアッ！」
lines.english: “Then stop me! Or kneel in disgrace! Hyaah!”

lines.japanese: やつは左の肘鉄を見せて俺を下がらせると同時に、腰をひねって横回転の溜めを入れた。俺の背筋に悪寒が走る。反対側の掌底がうなりをあげて戻ってきた。
lines.english: Showing me his left elbow to make me back off, he twisted his hips at the same time, winding up for a sideways turn. A chill ran down my spine. The heel of his other palm came roaring back.

lines.japanese: 冗談じゃない、あんなもの喰らったら確実に脳味噌が揺すぶられる。俺はとっさに顎を下げ、両腕の盾に頭を隠した。
lines.english: No fucking chance. A hit like that would rattle my brain. I dropped my chin and hid my head behind the shield of both arms.

lines.japanese: だが次の瞬間、俺はガード越しに、半握りのこぶしがばっくり開くのを見た。
lines.english: But in the next instant, through my guard, I saw his half-closed fist spring wide.
“Hahaa!”

lines.japanese: 開いた指が俺の左手首を掴んだ。熱い。握力が熱を帯びてる。その豪腕に引きよせられ、重心ごと俺のガードが下がった。
lines.english: His open fingers caught my left wrist. Hot. His grip felt hot. Dragged by that powerful arm, my guard dropped along with my center of gravity.

lines.japanese: 「ヤロウっ……！」
lines.english: “You bastard...!”

lines.japanese: 俺は前のめりになりながらも、右足を相手の体へ叩きつけた。中途半端なロー。相手の膝下を打ったが手応えが薄い。おまけに俺はそのせいで体勢を崩した。
lines.english: Even as I pitched forward, I slammed my right foot at his body. A half-assed low kick. It hit below his knee without much effect. Worse, it threw me off balance.
“Haa-hah!”

lines.japanese: 沈みゆく俺の目の前で、やつの膝が浮きあがった。来る。だが見切ることが出来ても、俺は腕を取られている上、傾く体に制動が効かない。
lines.english: As I sank, his knee rose before my eyes. It was coming. I read it, but he had my arm and there was no stopping my falling body.

lines.japanese: 腹に一撃来た。さっき手刀を喰らったところだ。内臓が圧迫されて息が漏れる。体の真ん中が鈍く痺れて力が抜けそうだ。
lines.english: A blow landed in my stomach. The same spot he’d hit with the edge of his hand. My insides were squeezed and my breath leaked out. The middle of my body went dully numb, and my strength threatened to drain away.

lines.japanese: だが急所じゃない。踏んばれる。俺は崩れおちる……素振りを見せて、自ら相手のふところに頭を潜りこませた。
lines.english: But it wasn’t a vital spot. I could hold on. I started to crumple... or pretended to, ducking my head inside his reach myself.
“Hrragh!”

lines.japanese: そして次の瞬間、渾身の力を込めて後頭部を振りあげた。
lines.english: In the next instant, I whipped the back of my head upward with all my strength.

lines.japanese: 「ぐっ！」
lines.english: “Ghh!”

lines.japanese: 鳳の顎を打ちぬき、その隙に乗じて腕を引き、束縛を振りほどく。
lines.english: It smashed into Ohtori’s chin. In that opening, I pulled my arm back and broke free.

lines.japanese: 「はあっ、はあっ……！」
lines.english: “Hah, hah...!”

lines.japanese: 形成逆転。俺は仰けぞった相手の胸倉を、片手で掴んで引きよせた。許せ、じいさん。こいつは立派な正当防衛だ。それに俺の狙いも急所じゃない。やつの薄らにやけた顔面だ。
lines.english: The tables turned. I caught the front of his coat in one hand as he arched backward and pulled him in. Forgive me, old man. This was self-defense, plain and simple. And I wasn’t aiming for a vital spot either. Just that faintly smirking face.
“Gah!”

lines.japanese: 肘を固めて、こぶしを傷めない程度のフックを横っ面にぶちこんだ。
lines.english: Locking my elbow, I drove a hook into the side of his face, measured so I wouldn't injure my fist.

lines.japanese: ついでに、俺が喰らったのと同じところへボディブローを一発。
lines.english: For good measure, I put one body blow into the same place he had struck me.

lines.japanese: 「おぶっ……」
やつは無様に膝をつく。遠巻きに野次馬たちがざわめいていた。
lines.english: He dropped to his knees in disgrace. The onlookers murmured from a distance.

lines.japanese: 逃げるなら、このときだった。
lines.english: This was my chance to run.

lines.japanese: しかし俺は、やつの理解しがたい言葉とただならぬ眼光が気にかかっていた。この男は、なぜ俺に絡んできたのだろう。
lines.english: But his incomprehensible words and extraordinary eyes were bothering me. Why had this man picked a fight with me?

lines.japanese: 「ハハハハ……！」
lines.english: “Hahahaha...!”

lines.japanese: 俺がファイティングポーズを取って見下ろしていると、鳳は優雅とも言える動きでやおら立ちあがった。ガムを噛むみたいに口をうごめかせたあと、赤い色の混じった唾液を吐きだす。
lines.english: As I looked down at him in my fighting stance, Ohtori slowly rose with a movement you could almost call graceful. He worked his mouth as if chewing gum, then spat out saliva tinged with red.

lines.japanese: 「ヘッ！　そんなもんじゃあねえよなあ？」
lines.english: “Heh! That’s not all you’ve gooot, is it?”

lines.japanese: 「なにが」
lines.english: “What isn’t?”

lines.japanese: 両足で地に立った鳳は、しかし、もう構えの姿勢を取らなかった。糸の切れたマリオネットみたいに首を傾け、またゆらゆらと体全体で揺れはじめた。
lines.english: On his feet again, Ohtori didn’t take a stance this time. Tilting his neck like a marionette with cut strings, he started swaying with his whole body again.

lines.japanese: 「甘めえだろ。違げえだろ。そうじゃねえだろ」
lines.english: “You’re going easy. That’s not it. That’s not how it is.”

lines.japanese: 「だから、なにが」
lines.english: “I said, what isn’t?”

lines.japanese: 気味が悪い。俺は臨戦態勢を解かずに一歩距離をあけた。
lines.english: Creepy bastard. I kept my guard up and opened the distance by one step.

lines.japanese: 「もっと晒けだせよ。俺が見届けてやる」
lines.english: “Show me more of yourself. I’ll bear witness.”

lines.japanese: やつの言葉が分からない。
lines.english: I didn’t understand what he was saying.

lines.japanese: しかし、イカレてるには違いないが、気になることを口にするやつだ。
lines.english: But crazy as he definitely was, he said things that got to me.

lines.japanese: 「あのさ。おまえ俺のこと知ってんの」
lines.english: “Listen. Do you know me?”

lines.japanese: 「知らねえよ。だが知ってることもある」
lines.english: “No. But there are things I know.”

lines.japanese: たしかに、いろんなところからいろんなやつが集まる柳木原には、ブッ壊れてるやつが少なくない。しかし、こういうタイプの馬鹿に遭遇したのは初めてだった。
lines.english: Sure, Yanagihara drew all kinds of people from all kinds of places, and plenty of them were broken. But this was my first time meeting this type of idiot.

lines.japanese: 「なんだそれ。手短に言え。早くしねーとお巡りさん呼ばれちゃうだろ」
lines.english: “What the hell does that mean? Keep it short. Somebody’s gonna call the cops if you take too long.”

lines.japanese: 睨みながらそう言うと、鳳は眉をひそめて笑った。
lines.english: I said it with a glare. Ohtori furrowed his brow and smiled.

lines.japanese: 「そう生きいそぐな。なんだ、警察が怖いのか？　なぜだろうなあ。おまえは被害者だ、目撃者もいる。いかに無能なデコスケでもおまえを罪には問わねえだろ」
lines.english: “Don’t be so eager to rush through life. What, scared of the police? Why’s thaaat? You’re the victim. There are witnesses. Even the most useless pig wouldn’t charge you.”

lines.japanese: 「っせえな、いいだろ。めんどくせー事情聴取とか職務質問とか、そんなん嫌いなんだよ」
lines.english: “Shut up. I hate all that pain-in-the-ass questioning and getting stopped in the street.”

lines.japanese: 「ほォ……なら場所を変えるか」
lines.english: “Ohhh... Then shall we go somewhere else?”

lines.japanese: やつはぎらぎらと暑苦しい笑みを残して背を向けた。筋肉質で幅の広い肩は、後ろから刺してもピンピンしてそうだ。
lines.english: He turned his back, leaving me with that blazing, overbearing grin. Those broad, muscular shoulders made him look like he’d shrug off a stab in the back.

lines.japanese: 「まだ所轄に目を付けられてないサイケ箱がある。音響は大したことねえが、クラブ黎明期の混沌としたアングラ臭を今に残す貴重な遊び場だ。日常を忘れるには具合がいいぜえ。来いよ」
lines.english: “There’s a psychedelic club the local cops haven’t got their eye on yet. The sound system’s nothing special, but it’s one of the few places left that still has that whiff of underground chaos from the early club scene. Good for forgetting everyday life. Come ooon.”

lines.japanese: 肩越しにこちらを振りかえり、威圧感たっぷりに形の良い顎をしゃくる。
lines.english: Looking back over his shoulder, he jerked his well-shaped chin at me, full of menace.

lines.japanese: 「来いよじゃねーよバカ。良い子は寝る時間だぞコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “Don’t ‘come on’ me, idiot. It’s bedtime for good little boys, you bastard.”

lines.japanese: 「ハ、構えるなよ、体育館裏で囲もうってわけじゃない。逆だ、仲間に紹介してやる」
lines.english: “Hah, don’t brace yourself. I’m not taking you behind the gym to get jumped. The opposite. I’ll introduce you to the others.”

lines.japanese: やつはふらりと体ごと振りかえった。笑っている。寝不足の作家みたいに充血した半眼。それは刃物を振りまわしていたときの不気味な笑顔と、どこか違うのだろうか。
lines.english: He let his whole body drift around. He was smiling. Half-lidded eyes, bloodshot as a sleepless writer's. Was this smile really any different from the sinister one he'd worn while waving a knife?

lines.japanese: 「俺の誘い、まさか断らねえよなあ？」
lines.english: “You’re not going to turn me dooown, are you?”

lines.japanese: 「断るに決まってんだろ、通り魔ヤロウ。ひとりで行けよ。俺は知らないおじさんに付いてっちゃいけないって、死んだじいさんに言われてんだよ」
lines.english: “Of course I’m turning you down, you knife-waving maniac. Go alone. Before he died, the old man told me not to go off with strange men.”

lines.japanese: 「つれねえなあ。挨拶が過激だったか？　つまんねえことで怒るやつだ」
lines.english: “So cold. Was my greeting a little intense? You get angry over such trivial things.”

lines.japanese: 「怒ってねーつってんだろ。元からこうなんだよ。悪かったな態度でかくて」
lines.english: “I told you, I’m not angry. I’ve always been like this. Sorry I’ve got an attitude.”

lines.japanese: 「奇遇だなあ。俺もだ」
lines.english: “What a coincidence. So have I.”

lines.japanese: 鳳はまた、視点を固定したまま斜めを向いた。ひとに頬を向けて話す癖があるみたいだ。
lines.english: Ohtori turned his face to an angle again without moving his eyes. Seemed he had a habit of talking to people with his cheek turned toward them.

lines.japanese: 「だが、わきまえない犬とおもねらない狼は違う。おまえは誇りたかい戦士だ。名を教えろ」
lines.english: “But a dog with no manners is different from a wolf that won’t grovel. You’re a proud warrior. Tell me your name.”

lines.japanese: 「あァ？　なんで赤の他人に個人情報流さなきゃなんねーんだよ」
lines.english: “Huh? Why should I hand personal information to a complete stranger?”

lines.japanese: 「他人じゃあねえだろ。古い青春ドラマを見たことはないか？　こぶしを交えたあとに友情が芽生えるなんて冗談も、ときには面白えと思わねえかあ？」
lines.english: “We're not strangers anymore. Never seen an old teen drama? Don't you find the old joke about friendship blossoming after an exchange of fists amusing now and then?”

lines.japanese: 友情、なんて言葉を聞いたのは久しぶりだった。
lines.english: It had been a long time since I’d heard the word “friendship.”

lines.japanese: 「それに、なあアミーゴ、先に俺の名を聞いたのはおまえの方だった。次はおまえの番だろう」
lines.english: “Besides, amigo, you asked my name first. Now it’s your turn.”

lines.japanese: やつは屁理屈を言う。俺は自分の名を告げていいものか迷った。
lines.english: His logic was pure bullshit. I hesitated over whether to give him my name.

lines.japanese: 「……成田隼人」
lines.english: “...Hayato Narita.”

lines.japanese: しかし結局はそれを口にしていた。
lines.english: Yet in the end, I heard myself say it.

lines.japanese: 「へえファルコンってわけだ」
lines.english: “Oh, so your name’s got a falcon in it.”

lines.japanese: やつのしかめ面が揺らいで、急に幼くなった気がした。
lines.english: Something in his scowl wavered. Suddenly he seemed younger.

lines.japanese: 「来いよ、隼人」
lines.english: “Come on, Hayato.”

lines.japanese: 「あァ？　てめ、なに気安く呼んでんだよ。つか命令すんじゃねーよ。つか行かねッつってんだろ」
lines.english: “Huh? Don't use my name like we're friends. And quit ordering me around. And I already said I'm not going.”

lines.japanese: 「なんだあ、酒が苦手ならカフェにするかあ？」
lines.english: “What, don’t like drinking? Shall we make it a caaafe?”

lines.japanese: 「っせーな、そういう問題じゃねンだよ。ほっとけよ。ねえんだよ、金がねえんだよ」
lines.english: “Shut up, that isn't the problem. Leave me alone. I haven't got any. Any money.”

lines.japanese: 「ハッ、案ずるな。俺の口座には、毎月ひとりで使いきれないほどの小金が湧く。ガキの一晩分ぐれえ恵んでやるよ」
lines.english: “Hah. Fear not. Every month, more pocket change than I can spend alone springs into my bank account. I can spare enough to pay one kid’s way for a night.”

lines.japanese: 「っせーな、冗談じゃねーっつの。てめえみたいなワケわかんねーやつの、ワケわかんねー施しなんか、ワケわかんねーまま受けられるかっつーの。テメなめんなよ、貧乏人の意地なめんなよ」
lines.english: “Shut up. Like I'd take some handout I don't understand from some guy I don't understand while I still don't understand a goddamn thing. Don't underestimate me. Don't underestimate a poor man's pride.”

lines.japanese: 「遠慮するなァ、心に錦を着せたって腹は膨れねえだろう」
lines.english: “Don't be shy. Pride may dress your heart in brocade, but it won't fill your stomach.”

lines.japanese: 「う、うるせえっつんだよ」
lines.english: “I-I said shut up.”

lines.japanese: ぎゅるるるる。しかし残念ながら、俺はそのときとても腹を空かしていた。
lines.english: Grrrrrrgle. Unfortunately, I was extremely hungry just then.

lines.japanese: そして残念ながら、じいさんは俺に「友達は選べ」って言葉を教えていなかった。
lines.english: And unfortunately, the old man had never taught me to choose my friends carefully.

lines.japanese: 「か、借りるだけだ……バイト代が出たらすぐ返す……」
lines.english: “I-I’m only borrowing it… I’ll pay you back the minute I get paid…”
